paragraphs.title: Testimony, uncleanness, and an oath made unintentionally

easy.question: What happens to a person who hears an oath, is a witness or knows something, but does not testify?
answers: He bears his iniquity
He becomes a priest
He is completely free of guilt
easy.explanation: The verse says, “if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.”

easy.question: What unclean things might a person touch according to these verses?
answers: Only unclean clothing
The carcass of an unclean animal, livestock, or creeping thing
Only unclean water
easy.explanation: The passage lists the carcasses of unclean beasts, cattle, and creeping things.

easy.question: What might a person swear to do according to verse 4?
answers: Only something he has already done
Only something involving sacrifices
Something evil or something good
easy.explanation: The verse speaks of swearing “to do evil, or to do good.”

medium.question: What is the result when a person knows testimony but does not give it?
answers: He bears his iniquity
He receives a blessing
He becomes unclean
medium.explanation: According to the verse, anyone who knows and does not testify bears his iniquity.

medium.question: In the phrase “if it be hidden from him,” what does “hidden” mean in context?
answers: He deliberately concealed it
He did not know or notice it at the time
He ran away from the unclean place
medium.explanation: The context indicates that the person was unaware of the uncleanness until he later learned of it.

medium.question: What do the person who touches uncleanness and the person who makes a forgotten oath have in common?
answers: Both are initially unaware, then learn of it and become guilty
Both must testify in court
Both touch the carcass of a creeping thing
medium.explanation: In both cases, the matter is hidden from the person, and after learning of it he is considered guilty.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the first case and the other cases in these verses?
answers: The first case requires a person to give testimony, rather than deal only with uncleanness or an oath
In the first case the person always touched a carcass
In the first case the person has no responsibility
challenge.explanation: The first case concerns someone who must testify about what he has heard, seen, or known; the others concern uncleanness or an oath.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the words “to do evil, or to do good”?
answers: Only an oath intended to cause harm counts
An oath may concern either a harmful or a beneficial action
It is forbidden to swear about any action
challenge.explanation: The verse includes both an evil action and a good action, so the responsibility applies to oaths of either kind.

challenge.question: What wording is repeated in the cases of uncleanness and the case of the oath?
answers: They all say that the person was a priest
They all say that the person gave testimony
In each case the matter was hidden from him, and afterward he knew and became guilty
challenge.explanation: The verses repeatedly describe the matter as hidden from the person, followed by his learning of it and becoming guilty.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the first case and the other cases in these verses?
answers: The first case requires a person to give testimony, rather than deal only with uncleanness or an oath
In the first case the person always touched a carcass
In the first case the person has no responsibility
questions.explanation: The first case concerns someone who must testify about what he has heard, seen, or known; the others concern uncleanness or an oath.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the words “to do evil, or to do good”?
answers: Only an oath intended to cause harm counts
An oath may concern either a harmful or a beneficial action
It is forbidden to swear about any action
questions.explanation: The verse includes both an evil action and a good action, so the responsibility applies to oaths of either kind.

questions.question: What wording is repeated in the cases of uncleanness and the case of the oath?
answers: They all say that the person was a priest
They all say that the person gave testimony
In each case the matter was hidden from him, and afterward he knew and became guilty
questions.explanation: The verses repeatedly describe the matter as hidden from the person, followed by his learning of it and becoming guilty.

paragraphs.title: Confession and bringing a sin offering

easy.question: What must a person do after sinning?
answers: Hide his sin
Confess his sin
Leave the camp
easy.explanation: The verse says, “he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing.”

easy.question: What must he bring to the Lord for his sin?
answers: A grain offering
Oil
A female animal from the flock
easy.explanation: The verse requires a female from the flock, such as a lamb or a female goat.

easy.question: Who makes atonement for the sinner?
answers: The priest
The sinner alone
The elders of the people
easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “the priest shall make an atonement for him.”

medium.question: What is the correct order of actions in these verses?
answers: The priest makes atonement, the person confesses, and then brings an offering
The person confesses, brings an offering, and the priest makes atonement
The person brings an offering, hides his sin, and the priest judges him
medium.explanation: First the person confesses, then brings the offering, and finally the priest makes atonement.

medium.question: What does “he shall be guilty” mean in context?
answers: He is guilty or liable
He will be joyful
He will be wealthy
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a person who has sinned and is therefore accountable.

medium.question: Why does the person bring the offering to the Lord?
answers: To celebrate his success
For his sin, so that atonement may be made
To replace the priest
medium.explanation: The offering is brought for his sin, and the priest then makes atonement for him.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “in one of these”?
answers: The person is guilty of one of the cases mentioned earlier
The person must bring every kind of offering
The person does not know what he has done
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers back to one of the cases described in the preceding verses.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “a female from the flock” tell us about the offering?
answers: It must be a male animal
It may only be a bird
It must be a female animal
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically requires a female animal from the flock, such as a lamb or female goat.

challenge.question: What difference between the roles of the person and the priest appears in the verse?
answers: The person confesses and brings the offering, while the priest makes atonement
The person makes atonement, while the priest confesses
Both of them only bring the offering
challenge.explanation: The person is responsible for confession and bringing the offering; the priest performs the atonement.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “in one of these”?
answers: The person is guilty of one of the cases mentioned earlier
The person must bring every kind of offering
The person does not know what he has done
questions.explanation: The phrase refers back to one of the cases described in the preceding verses.

questions.question: What does the phrase “a female from the flock” tell us about the offering?
answers: It must be a male animal
It may only be a bird
It must be a female animal
questions.explanation: The verse specifically requires a female animal from the flock, such as a lamb or female goat.

questions.question: What difference between the roles of the person and the priest appears in the verse?
answers: The person confesses and brings the offering, while the priest makes atonement
The person makes atonement, while the priest confesses
Both of them only bring the offering
questions.explanation: The person is responsible for confession and bringing the offering; the priest performs the atonement.

paragraphs.title: The offering of a poor person: birds

easy.question: What may a person bring if he cannot afford a lamb?
answers: A bull and a calf
Two turtledoves or two young pigeons
Two sheep
easy.explanation: Instead of a lamb, a person who cannot afford one may bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons.

easy.question: What is one of the birds designated for?
answers: A sin offering
A peace offering
A tithe
easy.explanation: The verse says that one bird is to be offered as a sin offering.

easy.question: Who offers the birds and carries out the offering procedure?
answers: The sinner
The king
The priest
easy.explanation: The person brings the birds to the priest, who offers them.

medium.question: Which offering is made first?
answers: The burnt offering
The sin offering
The peace offering
medium.explanation: The priest offers the bird for the sin offering first, and then the other bird as a burnt offering.

medium.question: What does “if he be not able to bring a lamb” mean in context?
answers: His hand was injured
He is not permitted to offer one
He cannot afford or obtain a lamb
medium.explanation: The context concerns a person who cannot bring a lamb, so the phrase refers to his financial ability.

medium.question: What is done with the blood of the sin offering?
answers: Some is sprinkled on the side of the altar and the rest is poured out at its base
All of it is poured outside the camp
All of it is burned on the altar
medium.explanation: The priest sprinkles some blood on the side of the altar and pours out the remainder at its bottom.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from bringing two birds with different purposes?
answers: Both birds are used for exactly the same action
The offering includes both a sin offering and a burnt offering, each with its own purpose
Only the first bird counts as an offering
challenge.explanation: The verses distinguish between the bird for the sin offering and the bird for the burnt offering.

challenge.question: What special instruction is given about removing the head of the sin-offering bird?
answers: The head must be separated completely
The head must not be touched
The head is to be removed without completely separating it
challenge.explanation: The head is to be wrung from the neck, but the verse says not to divide it completely.

challenge.question: What is the exact order leading to atonement and forgiveness?
answers: The sin offering is made, then the burnt offering, and the priest makes atonement and the person is forgiven
The burnt offering is made, then the sin offering, and afterward the person confesses
The blood is poured out, then the birds are brought, and finally the sin offering is made
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the sin offering first, the burnt offering second, and then atonement and forgiveness.

questions.question: What can be inferred from bringing two birds with different purposes?
answers: Both birds are used for exactly the same action
The offering includes both a sin offering and a burnt offering, each with its own purpose
Only the first bird counts as an offering
questions.explanation: The verses distinguish between the bird for the sin offering and the bird for the burnt offering.

questions.question: What special instruction is given about removing the head of the sin-offering bird?
answers: The head must be separated completely
The head must not be touched
The head is to be removed without completely separating it
questions.explanation: The head is to be wrung from the neck, but the verse says not to divide it completely.

questions.question: What is the exact order leading to atonement and forgiveness?
answers: The sin offering is made, then the burnt offering, and the priest makes atonement and the person is forgiven
The burnt offering is made, then the sin offering, and afterward the person confesses
The blood is poured out, then the birds are brought, and finally the sin offering is made
questions.explanation: The passage describes the sin offering first, the burnt offering second, and then atonement and forgiveness.

paragraphs.title: A grain offering for one who cannot afford the birds

easy.question: What does a person bring if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons?
answers: The tenth part of an ephah of fine flour
A lamb
Oil and frankincense
easy.explanation: A person who cannot afford the birds brings the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour.

easy.question: Who takes a handful of the flour and burns it on the altar?
answers: The sinner
The priest
The king
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the priest shall take his handful of it” and burn it.

easy.question: What is the result of the priest’s action?
answers: The person becomes a priest
The offering remains with the person
The person is atoned for and forgiven
easy.explanation: The passage concludes that the priest makes atonement and the person is forgiven.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: The person brings the offering, the priest takes a handful and burns it, and then there is atonement and forgiveness
The priest makes atonement, and afterward the person brings the offering
The person burns the offering, and then the priest brings the flour
medium.explanation: First the person brings the flour; then the priest takes a handful and burns it; afterward atonement and forgiveness are described.

medium.question: Why does the person bring flour instead of two birds?
answers: Because flour is more expensive
Because he cannot afford or obtain the birds
Because the priest asked him to change the offering
medium.explanation: The passage provides flour as an alternative for someone unable to bring the birds.

medium.question: What does “the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour” describe?
answers: A container full of oil
Part of the altar
A measure of fine flour equal to one-tenth of an ephah
medium.explanation: The phrase specifies both the amount and the substance of the offering.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from allowing flour instead of birds?
answers: The offering is available even to someone with limited means
Only wealthy people may bring offerings
The flour is intended only for priests
challenge.explanation: The passage provides an alternative for a person who cannot afford birds.

challenge.question: What distinguishes this flour offering from an ordinary grain offering?
answers: The person eats all of it
No oil or frankincense is to be added
It must not be brought to the priest
challenge.explanation: Because it is a sin offering, the verse says that no oil or frankincense is to be put on it.

challenge.question: What does “the remnant shall be the priest’s, as a meat offering” mean?
answers: The priest must return all the flour
The person eats all the flour
What remains of the offering belongs to the priest, as with a grain offering
challenge.explanation: After the memorial portion is burned, the remainder belongs to the priest.

questions.question: What can be inferred from allowing flour instead of birds?
answers: The offering is available even to someone with limited means
Only wealthy people may bring offerings
The flour is intended only for priests
questions.explanation: The passage provides an alternative for a person who cannot afford birds.

questions.question: What distinguishes this flour offering from an ordinary grain offering?
answers: The person eats all of it
No oil or frankincense is to be added
It must not be brought to the priest
questions.explanation: Because it is a sin offering, the verse says that no oil or frankincense is to be put on it.

questions.question: What does “the remnant shall be the priest’s, as a meat offering” mean?
answers: The priest must return all the flour
The person eats all the flour
What remains of the offering belongs to the priest, as with a grain offering
questions.explanation: After the memorial portion is burned, the remainder belongs to the priest.

paragraphs.title: Trespass against holy things and the trespass offering

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of this section?
answers: Moses
The priest
The people
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “And the Lord spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: What animal is brought for the trespass offering?
answers: A lamb or goat
A ram without blemish from the flock
A bull
easy.explanation: The verses require a ram without blemish from the flock.

easy.question: What happens after the priest makes atonement for the person?
answers: He must bring another offering
He is punished
He is forgiven
easy.explanation: The passage says, “and it shall be forgiven him.”

medium.question: What must someone do who sins unintentionally against the holy things of the Lord?
answers: Restore what was involved, add a fifth, give it to the priest, and bring a ram
Bring only a grain offering
Wait until he remembers his sin
medium.explanation: He must make restitution, add a fifth, give it to the priest, and bring a ram as a trespass offering.

medium.question: What does “commit a trespass” mean in this context?
answers: To rejoice
To trespass against or misuse what is holy
To forget
medium.explanation: The context concerns wrongdoing involving the holy things of the Lord.

medium.question: Why does a person bring an offering even when he did not know he had sinned?
answers: Because the priest made a legal mistake
Because everyone must bring an offering every day
Because an unintentional sin still brings guilt
medium.explanation: The passage says that even without knowing, the person is guilty and bears his iniquity.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the sin in verses 15–16 and the sin in verses 17–18?
answers: The first requires restitution and an added fifth, while the second concerns a sin of which the person was unaware
The first needs no priest, while the second requires only a grain offering
The first is deliberate, while the second is intentional
challenge.explanation: The first case involves misuse of holy things and restitution; the second describes a forbidden act done without the person knowing it.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated statement that the person did not know, yet still bears his iniquity?
answers: Only the priest can know whether a sin occurred
Lack of knowledge does not remove responsibility for sin
No atonement is needed when a person is unaware
challenge.explanation: The verses teach that an unintentional or unknown sin still requires atonement.

challenge.question: What does the closing statement “It is a trespass offering: he hath certainly trespassed against the Lord” emphasize?
answers: The offering belongs only to the priest
The sin has nothing to do with worship
The person is guilty before the Lord and therefore needs a trespass offering
challenge.explanation: The conclusion emphasizes both the seriousness of the guilt and its direct relation to the Lord.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the sin in verses 15–16 and the sin in verses 17–18?
answers: The first requires restitution and an added fifth, while the second concerns a sin of which the person was unaware
The first needs no priest, while the second requires only a grain offering
The first is deliberate, while the second is intentional
questions.explanation: The first case involves misuse of holy things and restitution; the second describes a forbidden act done without the person knowing it.

answers: Only the priest can know whether a sin occurred

questions.explanation: The verses teach that an unintentional or unknown sin still requires atonement.

answers: The offering belongs only to the priest
The sin has nothing to do with worship
The person is guilty before the Lord and therefore needs a trespass offering
questions.explanation: The conclusion emphasizes both the seriousness of the guilt and its direct relation to the Lord.

easy.question: What must a person do if he has taken another person’s property?
answers: Return the property
Hide it
Sell it
easy.explanation: The passage requires returning stolen property, goods held in trust, or lost property to its owner.

easy.question: What animal does the person bring as a trespass offering?
answers: A young goat
A ram without blemish
A dove
easy.explanation: The passage says that he must bring a ram without blemish from the flock.

easy.question: Who makes atonement after the person brings the trespass offering?
answers: The king
The witness who testified against him
The priest
easy.explanation: The final verse says that the priest makes atonement for him before the Lord.

medium.question: What is the correct order after a person sins in matters of property?
answers: Return the property, add a fifth, and then bring a trespass offering
Bring a trespass offering, and then decide whether to return the property
Add a fifth without returning the property
medium.explanation: He must first return the property, add a fifth of its value, and then bring the trespass offering.

medium.question: What does “property held in trust” mean in the phrase “deny his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep”?
answers: Something entrusted to him for safekeeping
A gift he received
A place where he prayed
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to property that another person gave him to guard or keep.

medium.question: Why does the person add a fifth to what he returns?
answers: To compensate the owner for the loss and delay
To buy another ram
To pay the priest alone
medium.explanation: Returning the principal plus a fifth provides compensation to the owner.

challenge.question: What detail shows that the sin harms both human relationships and the person’s relationship with the Lord?
answers: It is described as a trespass against the Lord and also involves wronging another person
Only the priest’s sacrifice is mentioned
The person is said to have found lost property
challenge.explanation: The passage calls the act a trespass against the Lord while describing harm done to another person’s property or rights.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the passage listing several forms of deception?
answers: Only violent theft is sinful
Denial, oppression, false swearing, and keeping lost property are also serious offenses
Only damage to temple property is forbidden
challenge.explanation: The examples show that moral responsibility includes deception and denial, not only obvious theft.

challenge.question: What practical condition accompanies the forgiveness described at the end?
answers: The person must deny what he did
The person must return the property and bring a trespass offering
The person must pay only a fifth without returning the principal
challenge.explanation: Forgiveness follows the repair of the wrong: returning the property, adding a fifth, and bringing a ram as a trespass offering.

answers: The person must deny what he did
The person must return the property and bring a trespass offering
The person must pay only a fifth without returning the principal
questions.explanation: Forgiveness follows the repair of the wrong: returning the property, adding a fifth, and bringing a ram as a trespass offering.
